messages:
jessica: quick question — hitting a weird mix of 407 (proxy auth) + TLS SNI errors when our Node SDK talks to the private VPC endpoint through corp HTTP proxy. We set REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://redwood.internal.svc and the proxy is doing host-rewrite. Streaming responses start then stall after ~3s. anyone seen this pattern?

omar: can you paste the minimal client config you're using? also is the proxy an HTTP CONNECT tunnel (tunneling TLS) or a plain forward proxy that terminates TLS? those behave very differently.

jessica: minimal repro:

```js
// env
process.env.REDWOOD_BASE_URL = 'https://redwood.internal.svc';
process.env.HTTPS_PROXY = 'http://corp-proxy:3128';

// request
await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'redwood-small', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }], stream: true });
```

proxy is a plain forward proxy that our infra requires. if i unset HTTPS_PROXY it works (but obviously can't in prod).

kevin: forwarding proxies that rewrite Host will break TLS SNI or certificate validation unless the client tunnels via CONNECT. Node's https agents need a tunneling agent for that. Try https-proxy-agent or tunnel-agent and ensure you're establishing a CONNECT before TLS handshake. example: `const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTPS_PROXY)` and pass `fetch(..., { agent })` or SDK config if it accepts an `agent` option.

Also streaming stalls can be caused by the proxy buffering chunked responses; some proxies buffer until the response is complete. If the proxy is doing response buffering, you won't get streaming.

omar: adding: check Host vs :authority. Many proxies rewrite the Host header to the proxy's hostname. You can try setting an explicit Host header that matches the private endpoint host so upstream sees the expected vhost, e.g. `Host: redwood.internal.svc`. If the proxy drops that you'll need a tunneling CONNECT.

kevin: quick curl to validate behaviour (run from a host that uses the proxy):

```bash
# will use proxy and attempt to tunnel
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:3128 --proxy-tunnel https://redwood.internal.svc/v1/chat/stream
# or without tunnel to see buffering
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:3128 https://redwood.internal.svc/v1/chat/stream
```

erin: fwiw, Python folks: requests and httpx follow env proxies by default. For httpx async streaming behind a proxy you often need `trust_env=False` and then supply an explicit `proxies=` mapping with `http://` -> `http://corp-proxy:3128` or use `httpx.Client(http2=True, proxies=...)`. If you need mTLS, the private endpoint expects the original Host header and SNI — so a tunnel is required.

sre-bot: Note: internal doc updated: /devex/private-endpoints/proxy-behavior — section on "tunnel vs forward proxy" and SDK agent knobs.

jessica: thanks — two followups: 1) does Redwood SDK expose an "agent" or "transport" option for Node so we can inject HttpsProxyAgent? 2) any recommended headers (X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Proto) we should set when proxying for telemetry?

kevin: 1) Node SDK: yes, the client constructor accepts `fetchOptions` / `httpAgent` in the client config in recent versions — check changelog 2.8+. If not, wrap `globalThis.fetch` with a small wrapper that uses agent. 2) set `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-For` for observability, but do not rely on them for routing. For private vhost routing you want SNI/Host to match the upstream certificate.

omar: small gotcha — trailing slash on REDWOOD_BASE_URL can cause path join issues when proxy rewrites. prefer no trailing slash: `https://redwood.internal.svc` not `https://redwood.internal.svc/` (some SDKs will concat `/v1` producing `//v1`).

jessica: perfect. i'll try HttpsProxyAgent + explicit Host header and report back. thanks all :thumbsup:
